title: Home inspector lead disclosure: which sales and leases it covers practice questions
description: Practice questions on which sales and leases the federal lead disclosure rule covers: target housing, exceptions, exempt deals, terms (40 CFR 745.100-103).

questions.question: A studio apartment built in 1970 is being leased to a family whose 3-year-old child will live there. Under 40 CFR 745.103, is the apartment target housing?

options.A: No, because a studio apartment is always excluded as a 0-bedroom dwelling
options.B: No, because only sales, not leases, can involve target housing
options.C: Yes, because a child who is less than 6 years of age is expected to reside in it
options.D: Yes, but only if the lease runs longer than one year

questions.explanation: The 0-bedroom exception applies "unless any child who is less than 6 years of age resides or is expected to reside in such housing."

questions.question: Under 745.103, what makes a residential dwelling a "0-bedroom dwelling"?

options.A: The living area is not separated from the sleeping area
options.B: The dwelling has no separate kitchen
options.C: The dwelling is rented to a single occupant
options.D: The dwelling has no closets in the sleeping area

questions.explanation: A 0-bedroom dwelling is "any residential dwelling in which the living area is not separated from the sleeping area."

questions.question: Under 745.103, "housing for the elderly" is housing reserved for households of one or more persons of what age or more at the time of initial occupancy?

options.A: 50 years
options.B: 55 years
options.C: 70 years
options.D: 62 years

questions.explanation: Housing for the elderly is reserved for households "composed of one or more persons 62 years of age or more at the time of initial occupancy."

questions.question: A three-bedroom house built in 1958 is sold at a foreclosure sale. How does 745.101 treat that sale?

options.A: It is covered, because the lender is a seller under 745.103
options.B: It is one of the exceptions: 745.101(a) lists sales of target housing at foreclosure
options.C: It is covered only if a child under 6 lives in the house
options.D: It is covered, but the purchaser's evaluation period is shortened

questions.explanation: Subpart F "applies to all transactions to sell or lease target housing, including subleases, with the exception of the following:" and 745.101(a) lists "Sales of target housing at foreclosure."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: How does 745.103 define "foreclosure"?

options.A: Any of the various methods of enforcing payment of a debt by the taking and selling of real property
options.B: Any sale in which the purchaser pays the full price in cash
options.C: Any transfer of housing between members of the same family
options.D: Any sale of housing that has stood vacant for a year or more

questions.explanation: Foreclosure means methods "of enforcing payment of a debt, by the taking and selling of real property."

questions.question: A landlord leases a two-bedroom beach cottage built in 1960 for 90 days, and the lease lets the tenant extend for another 90 days. Is the lease excepted under 745.101(c)?

options.A: Yes, because the first term is 100 days or less
options.B: Yes, because vacation rentals are always excepted
options.C: No, because the short-term exception covers leases of 100 days or less only where no lease renewal or extension can occur
options.D: No, because only leases longer than 100 days are excepted

questions.explanation: 745.101(c) excepts "Short-term leases of 100 days or less, where no lease renewal or extension can occur." This lease can be extended, so that exception does not fit it.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.101(b), a lease of target housing is excepted when the housing has been found to be lead-based paint free by whom?

options.A: The lessor, after a visual check of the painted surfaces
options.B: An inspector certified under the Federal certification program or under a federally accredited State or tribal certification program
options.C: The local building department, when it issues a certificate of occupancy
options.D: The lessee, using a store-bought test kit

questions.explanation: The exception covers housing "found to be lead-based paint free by an inspector certified under the Federal certification program or under a federally accredited State or tribal certification program."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.101(b), what option does the lessor have about a prior finding that housing is lead-based paint free?

options.A: Replacing the finding with a signed statement of the lessor's own
options.B: Asking the lessee to waive the finding in writing
options.C: Extending the finding to other buildings without testing
options.D: Using the results of additional test(s) by a certified inspector to confirm or refute the prior finding

questions.explanation: "The lessor has the option of using the results of additional test(s) by a certified inspector to confirm or refute a prior finding."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.101(d), when is the renewal of an existing lease in target housing excepted?

options.A: When the lessee has lived in the housing for more than three years
options.B: When the rent stays the same as under the existing lease
options.C: When the lessee signs a waiver of the disclosure
options.D: When the lessor has previously disclosed all information required under § 745.107 and no new information described in § 745.107 has come into the lessor's possession

questions.explanation: Renewals are excepted where "the lessor has previously disclosed all information required under § 745.107 and where no new information described in § 745.107 has come into the possession of the lessor."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: For the renewal exception in 745.101(d), what does "renewal" include?

options.A: Both renegotiation of existing lease terms and/or ratification of a new lease
options.B: Only an automatic extension with unchanged terms
options.C: Only a renewal signed by the same lessee
options.D: Only a renewal for a term of one year or less

questions.explanation: "renewal shall include both renegotiation of existing lease terms and/or ratification of a new lease."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.101, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.102, on what date did the requirements take effect for owners of more than four residential dwellings?

options.A: January 1, 1978
options.B: March 6, 1995
options.C: September 6, 1996
options.D: June 1, 2000

questions.explanation: 745.102(a): "For owners of more than four residential dwellings, the requirements shall take effect on September 6, 1996."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.102, Effective dates (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A mortgagee holds legal title to target housing as collateral for a mortgage loan. Under 745.103, who is the owner?

options.A: The mortgagee
options.B: The mortgagor
options.C: The title insurance company
options.D: The local tax authority

questions.explanation: Where a mortgagee holds legal title as collateral for a mortgage loan, "the owner would be the mortgagor."

questions.topic: Sellers, lessors, agents and other parties
questions.question: Under 745.103, which entity is also included in the term "seller"?

options.A: An entity that transfers shares in a cooperatively owned project, in return for consideration
options.B: A lender that makes a mortgage loan on the housing
options.C: A lessee who renews a lease
options.D: A purchaser who signs a contract to buy the housing

questions.explanation: 745.103 says the term seller also includes "An entity that transfers shares in a cooperatively owned project, in return for consideration".

questions.topic: Sellers, lessors, agents and other parties
questions.question: Under 745.103, the term "agent" excludes purchasers and any purchaser's representative who receives all compensation from which party?

options.A: The seller
options.B: The lessor
options.C: The seller's representative
options.D: The purchaser

questions.explanation: The term agent "does not apply to purchasers or any purchaser's representative who receives all compensation from the purchaser."

questions.topic: Sellers, lessors, agents and other parties
questions.question: A housing agency offers apartments that are target housing for rent. Under 745.103, what is the housing agency?

options.A: A lessee
options.B: A lessor
options.C: A purchaser
options.D: An agent

questions.explanation: A lessor is "any entity that offers target housing for lease, rent, or sublease," including "housing agencies."

questions.question: Which condition fits the 745.103 definition of a "lead-based paint hazard"?

options.A: A condition that causes exposure to radon gas in a basement
options.B: A condition that causes exposure to asbestos fibers from pipe insulation
options.C: A condition that causes exposure to lead from lead-contaminated dust that would result in adverse human health effects
options.D: A condition that causes exposure to mold on a bathroom ceiling

questions.explanation: A lead-based paint hazard is "any condition that causes exposure to lead from lead-contaminated dust, lead-contaminated soil, or lead-contaminated paint" that would result in adverse human health effects.

questions.question: In Subpart F, what does "evaluation" mean?

options.A: A home appraisal for the purchaser's lender
options.B: A risk assessment and/or inspection
options.C: A walk-through by the seller before closing
options.D: Measures to reduce or eliminate exposure to lead-based paint hazards

questions.explanation: 745.103: "Evaluation means a risk assessment and/or inspection."

questions.question: Under 745.103, what is an "inspection"?

options.A: An on-site investigation to determine and report the existence, nature, severity, and location of lead-based paint hazards
options.B: Measures designed to reduce or eliminate human exposure to lead-based paint hazards
options.C: A portion of a building generally accessible to all residents/users
options.D: A surface-by-surface investigation to determine the presence of lead-based paint, and the provision of a report explaining the results

questions.explanation: An inspection is "A surface-by-surface investigation to determine the presence of lead-based paint" and "The provision of a report explaining the results of the investigation."

questions.question: Under 745.103, a risk assessment includes information gathering on what?

options.A: The age and history of the housing and occupancy by children under age 6
options.B: The purchaser's income and credit history
options.C: The market value of nearby homes
options.D: The seller's homeowner's insurance claims

questions.explanation: A risk assessment includes "Information gathering regarding the age and history of the housing and occupancy by children under age 6".

questions.topic: What the rule is and what it covers
questions.question: A buyer is purchasing a house built in 1979. According to EPA's Title X page, why does the disclosure rule not cover it?

options.A: Because only homes where a child under 6 lives are covered
options.B: Because HUD, not EPA, handles disclosure for newer homes
options.C: Because the Consumer Product Safety Commission banned residential lead-based paint in 1978
options.D: Because newer homes must be tested for lead before every sale instead

questions.explanation: EPA's page says the rule does not apply to "Housing built after 1977 (this rule does not cover post-1977 housing since the Consumer Product Safety Commission banned residential lead-based paint in 1978)".

source.title: EPA: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure Rule (Section 1018 of Title X) (retrieved Nov 15, 2026)
